sources.citation: KIRTADS (Kerala Institute for Research Training & Development Studies of SC/ST), kirtads.kerala.gov.in: Books, Reports, Journals and Scheduled Tribes pages (Malayalam; read online 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No Kalanadi-specific publication listed; tribal-language titles are Paniya, Kattunaikkan, Koraga, Kani, Muthuvan primers plus generic 'Gothrabhasha vyakaranam' (P.N. Raveendran 2017) and 'Gothrabhasha vyakaranavum nighanduvum' (C.G. Shyama 2018) whose language coverage is not stated. Kalanadi does not appear in the site's list of 36 Scheduled Tribes.

sources.citation: SPPEL (Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages, CIIL Mysuru) language list and language-documentation pages, sppel.org (read online 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Kalanadi is not among the 117 SPPEL languages (Kerala entries: Aranadan, Eravallan, Kadar, Kanikkar, Kudiya, Malasar, Malayan, Mannan, Muduga, Muthuvan, Paliya, Thachanadan Moopan, Urali etc.); no Kalanadi material.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Kalanadi [wkl]' (Wayback Machine capture 2016-03-05).
sources.note: Nothing; no Typology field. Population 750 (2004 survey), lexical-similarity percentages, vitality note, 'Unwritten'.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13:7 (July 2013). [10-page opening extract: preface, contents, Adiya sketch]
sources.note: Does not treat Kalanadi at all: contents list 13 languages (Adiya, Aranadan, Bettakurumba, Cholanaickan, Irula, Kakkala, Kani, Kurichiya, Malamuthan, Malaveda, Mannan, Muduga, Mullukurumba). No stress statements in the part read.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (Barb Waugh, SIL International). 2006. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, Change Request Number 2006-003: create [wkl] Kalanadi (adopted 2007-07-18). 7 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only prosody-adjacent remark (p.3, second-hand): 'Menon refers to this language as a dialect of Malayalam "with a peculiar intonation".' Sources cited: Jose Mathew et al. 2004 unpublished NLCI sociolinguistic survey of Wayanad (lexical similarity only); Menon (ed.) 1996 Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes vol. 2; Damodaran 1974; Iyer 1968.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: wkl Kalanadi (associated with CR 2006-003). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; gives ~750 speakers, lexical similarity (88% Pathiya, 81% Kunduvadi, 75% Malayalam), 'none' under written literature/recordings, and lists no dictionaries or grammars.
